question: Should OpenClaw allow sandboxed requester sessions to initiate ACP harness sessions through an opt-in bridge or placement contract, and which boundary should own spawn, steer, and cancel?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally crosses from a sandboxed session into host-side harness execution, so code inspection can prove the limitation but cannot choose the acceptable threat model or product contract.

options.title: Design an opt-in bridge
options.body: Define a narrow sandbox-to-ACP bridge with operator opt-in, requester/agent allowlists, audit logs, rate limits, docs, and live Docker/acpx proof before implementation.

options.title: Fold into execution backends
options.body: Defer this issue into the broader execution backend/profile design so ACP, subagents, containers, and Kubernetes share one placement model.

options.title: Keep ACP host-only
options.body: Maintain the current fail-closed policy and document that sandboxed sessions must use native subagents or run harnesses inside their container.

recommendation.title: Design an opt-in bridge
recommendation.body: Define a narrow sandbox-to-ACP bridge with operator opt-in, requester/agent allowlists, audit logs, rate limits, docs, and live Docker/acpx proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This account authored the current docs limitation and slash-command hardening and has the strongest recent history across the ACP spawn surface.
